raw_review_excerpt:
The plan is well-grounded: the core diagnosis (implement-tasks line 45 forces Claude via model-name inference) is verified in code, the proposed fix (workflow-level `provider: codex` + `modelReasoningEffort: xhigh`) aligns with existing schema and the piv-loop-codex precedent, and the phase-gated rollout is responsible. Main gaps: incomplete command enumeration (6 of ~14 classified), no transfer-rules distinguishing interactive piv-loop patterns from autonomous plan-to-pr, and a few missing validation guards.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] Incomplete command classification
- 2. [WARN] Interactive-vs-autonomous pattern transfer not specified
- 3. [WARN] Per-node model string can override workflow-level provider
- 4. [NOTE] xhigh reasoning effort has no enforcement guard
- 5. [NOTE] Bundle generator not named in Phase 4
- 6. [NOTE] Plan/artifact path convention (.claude/) not addressed

issues.title: Incomplete command classification
issues.details: The variant table names 6 commands needing Codex adaptations, but the baseline workflow has ~14 distinct command/script nodes. The remaining nodes (plan-setup, confirm-plan, validate, compose-finalize-pr, github-pr, sync, error-handling, test-coverage, comment-quality, synthesize) are implicitly assumed provider-neutral without verification. Several of these (e.g., confirm-plan, synthesize, error-handling) likely contain Claude-flavored prompt language that could leak assumptions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a full command classification table: every baseline node → provider-neutral | requires-codex-variant | script/removed. Verify each by grepping for Claude-specific language.

issues.title: Interactive-vs-autonomous pattern transfer not specified
issues.details: The plan uses archon-piv-loop-codex as a 'pattern library' but that workflow is interactive (loop nodes, gate_message, <promise> signal contracts). archon-plan-to-pr is autonomous. The plan never specifies which patterns transfer and which don't. Risk: signal contracts or interactive gate patterns copy-pasted into autonomous nodes where they have no effect.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short section: 'Transfer from piv-loop-codex: prompt discipline, per-file staging, stop discipline. Do NOT transfer: signal contracts, gate_message, interactive loop structures.'

issues.title: Per-node model string can override workflow-level provider
issues.details: model-validation.ts:15-24 shows inferProviderFromModel iterates built-in registrations first. If any Codex workflow node accidentally retains a Claude model string (e.g., from copy-paste), the inference will route that node to Claude despite workflow-level provider: codex. The plan's Phase 2 grep check partially addresses this, but Phase 3 ('runtime guardrails') should include an explicit validation rule: no node in the Codex workflow may have a model string that infers to a non-Codex provider.
issues.suggested_fix: Add to Phase 2/3 verification: `rg 'model:' archon-plan-to-pr-codex.yaml | grep -v codex` plus a note that workflow validation should warn when node model inference contradicts workflow provider.

issues.title: xhigh reasoning effort has no enforcement guard
issues.details: Plan says 'keep reasoning effort at xhigh' but doesn't specify whether validation must assert no node silently downgrades it. Per-node modelReasoningEffort can override workflow-level default (dag-node.ts:167).
issues.suggested_fix: Add to Phase 2 verification: `rg 'modelReasoningEffort:' archon-plan-to-pr-codex.yaml` — only the workflow-level xhigh should appear; no per-node overrides unless explicitly justified.

issues.title: Bundle generator not named in Phase 4
issues.details: Phase 4 says 'regenerate bundled defaults' but doesn't name the generator script (scripts/generate-bundled-defaults.ts) or the check command (bun run check:bundled). The bundled-defaults test will fail without regeneration.
issues.suggested_fix: Phase 4 should include: `bun run scripts/generate-bundled-defaults.ts` followed by `bun run check:bundled` before running the test.

issues.title: Plan/artifact path convention (.claude/) not addressed
issues.details: archon-piv-loop-codex writes plans to .claude/archon/plans/ (Claude-branded path). The plan covers CLAUDE.md vs AGENTS.md compatibility but is silent on whether artifact paths should change for the Codex workflow. Likely non-blocking since plan-to-pr consumes an existing plan via $ARTIFACTS_DIR, but docs-impact and review artifacts may still reference .claude/ paths.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a note acknowledging .claude/ artifact paths are inherited repo convention, not Claude-provider-specific, and do not need renaming for the Codex workflow.

review.best_case: The core direction is solid and code-verified. If the enumeration gaps are filled (full command classification, transfer rules, model-string guard), this plan produces a clean Codex-native workflow with no Claude provider leaks, an honest relationship to CLAUDE.md, and a rigorous side-by-side evaluation design. The phase-gated approach means each step is independently verifiable before the comparative evaluation run, which is the right sequencing for a first Codex plan-to-PR lane.
strongest_objections: The variant table covers only 6 of ~14 baseline nodes. Without classifying all commands, Phase 2 scope is unbounded and silent Claude assumptions could leak through unclassified commands like confirm-plan, validate, synthesize, error-handling, test-coverage, and comment-quality.

inferProviderFromModel (model-validation.ts:15-24) means a per-node Claude model string will override workflow-level provider: codex. The plan's static grep partially catches this, but there is no proposed runtime or validation-time guard against provider inference contradicting the workflow provider.

The piv-loop-codex 'pattern library' is an interactive workflow with signal contracts and gate messages; plan-to-pr is autonomous. Without explicit transfer rules, there is risk of copying interactive patterns into autonomous nodes where they are inert or confusing.
hidden_assumptions: All unclassified baseline commands (plan-setup, confirm-plan, validate, compose-finalize-pr, sync, error-handling, test-coverage, comment-quality, synthesize) are assumed provider-neutral without verification
Workflow-level provider: codex is assumed to prevent all Claude routing, but model-validation.ts shows per-node model strings can override this via built-in provider inference
archon-piv-loop-codex patterns are assumed transferable to an autonomous workflow without acknowledging the interactive/autonomous structural difference
.claude/ artifact paths are inherited as repo convention but never explicitly acknowledged as provider-independent
The Codex executor is assumed to respect modelReasoningEffort: xhigh in practice (schema acceptance ≠ runtime behavior)
review.what_would_change_my_mind: If inspecting the remaining ~13 baseline command prompts revealed that most contain deep Claude-specific language (TodoWrite, Claude model references, CLAUDE.md-as-compliance-surface framing), the scope of Phase 2 would be significantly larger than the plan implies, and the 6-command variant table would be materially misleading. That would move the incomplete-enumeration issue from WARN to BLOCK because Phase 2 effort would be unbounded. Conversely, if most commands are genuinely provider-neutral prompts, the current plan is close to ready as-is.
